subject: Business Models
title: Community-Owned Businesses
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Community-Owned Businesses.

hook.text: Green Bay Packers are owned by 360,000 fans. No billionaire owner. The community is the business model.

buildup.text: Community ownership uses cooperatives, shared equity, or crowdfunding to distribute control among members.

discovery.text: REI (co-op), Mondragon (worker-owned), and credit unions all prove that community-owned models can scale.

twist.text: Community-owned businesses grow slower because decisions require consensus. Speed is traded for alignment.

climax.text: As trust in big corporations declines, community ownership gains appeal as an alternative to shareholder capitalism.

punchline.text: 360,000 fan-owners, no billionaire. Community ownership trades speed for trust.

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off in community-owned business models?
options: Slower growth due to consensus-based decisions

details.summary: Community-owned businesses are funded and governed by their customers, members, or local communities rather than outside investors. Credit unions, food cooperatives, community-owned pubs in the UK.
details.whyItMatters: Frustration with extractive corporate practices is driving renewed interest in community ownership models. These businesses prioritize stakeholder value over shareholder returns.
takeaways: Members fund, own, and govern the business through democratic processes
Community ownership prioritizes stakeholder value over maximum profit
Credit unions, co-ops, and platform cooperatives are established examples

faq.question: What makes community-owned businesses different from investor-owned ones?
faq.answer: Decision-making is democratic with one member one vote rather than proportional to capital invested. Profits are distributed to members or reinvested in the community. The business serves member needs rather than maximizing returns for outside investors..

faq.question: Can community-owned businesses compete with investor-funded companies?
faq.answer: In some sectors they thrive: credit unions hold over 2 trillion in assets. However, limited access to growth capital restricts rapid scaling. Community businesses often compete by providing better service and local focus rather than lowest prices, maintaining loyal member bases.
